symptoms_or_prerequisites: at least 2 of: nausea, vomiting, rash, aches and pains, positive tourniquet test, leucopenia (WBC <5000/mm3)
recommended_action: Classify as 'Dengue without warning signs'
exclusions: any warning sign present -> upgrade to 'Dengue with warning signs'
evidence_passage: Dengue without warning signs: Fever (2-7 days) with two or more of the followings; nausea, vomiting, rash, aches and pains, positive tourniquet tests, or leucopenia (WBC <5000/mm3)
linked_facts: Warning signs list p.3 (main guideline p.28)

recommended_action: Classify as 'Dengue with warning signs' and manage as high risk
evidence_passage: Warning signs of dengue fever: Intense continuous abdominal pain or pain when palpating abdomen; Persistent vomiting (>=3 episodes in 1 hr or >=4 in 6 hrs); Fluid accumulation (pleural effusion, ascites, or pericardial effusion); Mucosal bleeding; Altered mental status; Hepatomegaly (>=2cm below costal margin); Progressive increase of the haematocrit

recommended_action: Use differentiating findings: dengue more likely with thrombocytopenia, rising haematocrit, leukopenia; chikungunya more likely with arthralgias; zika more likely with pruritus
exclusions: clinical findings alone cannot reliably distinguish - use laboratory confirmation
evidence_passage: HIGH (findings that differentiate them) - Dengue: Thrombocytopenia, Progressive increase in hematocrit, Leukopenia; Chikungunya: Arthralgias; Zika: Pruritus

recommended_action: Perform CBC, Haematocrit, Dengue NS1 antigen, SGOT, SGPT at first consultation to establish baseline
evidence_passage: Within 5 days: CBC, Haematocrit, Dengue NS1 antigen, SGOT, SGPT. These tests should be done during first consultation to get the baseline characteristics like Haematocrit and complete blood count if the patient presented within 5 days of fever.
linked_facts: NS1 positive day 1, may become negative day 4-5 p.6

recommended_action: Perform CBC and Dengue Antibody (IgM/IgG) test; IgM detectable after day 5, peaks day 7
evidence_passage: CBC and NS1 Ag up to day 5 and CBC and Dengue Antibody from day 6 onward will support the diagnosis

recommended_action: Monitor haematocrit at least twice daily during leakage period; a rise >10% indicates starting leakage and >20% from baseline indicates established leakage; monitor 3-hourly or more often in severe dengue/shock
exclusions: haematocrit may not rise if concomitant concealed or overt bleeding
evidence_passage: Rising haematocrit more than 10% indicates starting plasma leakage and rising haematocrit by 20% from the baseline indicates established plasma leakage... In critical phase/leaking phase haematocrit may not rise due to concomitant concealed or overt bleeding. During plasma leakage period Hct should be monitored at least twice daily
linked_facts: Baseline Hct assumptions (child 35%, adult female 38%, adult male 40%) p.5

symptoms_or_prerequisites: suspected dengue with clinical signs of fluid accumulation
recommended_action: Chest X-ray for pleural effusion; ultrasonography for pleural effusion/ascites; consider POC ultrasound (gallbladder wall thickening, peri-cholecystic fluid, hepato-renal pouch fluid, right pleural fluid, pelvic fluid)
exclusions: POC ultrasound not essential but useful
evidence_passage: Chest X-Ray: Pleural effusion on X-ray in dengue indicates fluid accumulation. Ultrasonography: To detect pleural effusions or ascites, it is essential to obtain objective evidence of selective capillary plasma leaking into the chest and abdominal cavities.
linked_facts: POC ultrasound areas of interest p.8-9

symptoms_or_prerequisites: no pre-existing liver or kidney disease
recommended_action: Paracetamol for temperature control: do not exceed 3 g/day in adults; 60 mg/kg/24h in children; tepid sponging as adjunct
exclusions: exceeding maximum dose
concurrent NSAIDs or steroids
evidence_passage: Control of temperature - Tepid sponging for fever - Do not exceed 3g/m day of paracetamol. (60mg/kg/24hrs in child) - Warn the patient that the fever may not fully settle with paracetamol and advise not to take excess.
linked_facts: Avoid all NSAIDS and steroids p.12

recommended_action: Avoid all NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors) and steroids; temporarily withhold warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel and dipyridamole; seek expert opinion where these drugs are essential
evidence_passage: Avoid all NSAIDS (including COX-2 inhibitors) and steroids. Temporally withhold warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel & dipyridamole, in patients who take these on long term basis. Take expert opinion where these drugs are necessary.
linked_facts: High-risk list includes patients on anticoagulants p.10

recommended_action: Home management: physical rest under mosquito net; tepid sponging; oral fluids ~2400 mL/24h (2 mL/kg/h if <50 kg); encourage urine every 3-4 h; light nutritious food; review daily with CBC from day 3 of fever; follow up until afebrile 24-48 h
exclusions: presence of warning signs
high-risk comorbidity
adverse social condition
pregnancy
evidence_passage: Ensure adequate oral fluid intake of around 2400 ml for 24 hours (if the body weight is less than 50kg, give fluids as 2ml/kg/hour for 24 hours)... Encourage to pass urine every 3-4 hours... First CBC should be done at least at the beginning of the third day of fever/illness... These patients should be followed up until the patient become afebrile for 24-48 hours with stable clinical parameters.

recommended_action: Return immediately if: clinical deterioration with settling of fever, inability to tolerate oral fluids, severe abdominal pain, lethargy/irritability/restlessness, bleeding tendency, reduced urine output (<150-200 mL/4-6h if >=50 kg), cold clammy extremities, difficulty breathing
evidence_passage: Advise patients to return to the hospital immediately, if they develop any of the following conditions: Clinical deterioration with settling of fever; Inability to tolerate oral fluids; Severe abdominal pain; Lethargy or irritability / restlessness; Bleeding tendency like abnormal vaginal bleeding, blood vomiting, black tarry stool, bleeding from nose and gum; Reduced urine output for the last 4-6 hours (<150-200 ml/4-6 hours if weight is 50kg or more); Cold and clammy extremities; Difficulty in breathing.
linked_facts: Settling of fever is not a sign of recovery p.11

recommended_action: Confirm diagnosis with repeated office visits: at least 3 measurements per visit, 2-3 visits at 1-4 week intervals; confirm with out-of-office BP (HBPM/ABPM) if available
exclusions: single-visit diagnosis not valid unless BP >=160/100 or HMOD present
evidence_passage: The diagnosis of hypertension should be based on at least three blood pressure measurements per visit and at least two to three visits at 1-4-week intervals... The diagnosis might be made on a single visit, if BP is >=160/100 mmHg or there is accompanying evidence of hypertension mediated organ damage (HMOD)

symptoms_or_prerequisites: symptoms of postural hypotension (falls or postural dizziness)
recommended_action: Measure postural BP: lying 5 min, standing at 1 and 3 min; abnormal if SBP drops >=20 mmHg or DBP drops >=10 mmHg or symptoms occur; review medication if abnormal
evidence_passage: A drop in SBP of >=20 mmHg, or in DBP of >=10 mmHg, or experiencing lightheadedness or dizziness on standing is considered abnormal and indicates postural hypotension... If the systolic BP falls by >=20 mmHg when the person is standing, medication is to be reviewed

recommended_action: Limited baseline investigations: serum sodium, potassium, creatinine and eGFR; lipid profile and fasting glucose if available; urine dipstick; 12-lead ECG; haemoglobin/haematocrit; chest X-ray; echocardiogram
exclusions: do not delay treatment if tests unavailable in low-resource settings
evidence_passage: All hypertensive patients should undergo a limited number of investigations... Sodium, potassium, serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR); If available lipid profile and fasting glucose; Urine analysis: Dipstick urine test; 12-lead ECG... Haemoglobin and/or haematocrit; Chest X-ray... Echocardiogram

recommended_action: Fundoscopy to detect hypertensive retinopathy (haemorrhages/exudates with or without papilloedema)
evidence_passage: Fundoscopy: To detect hypertensive retinopathy, especially in patients with grade 2 or 3 hypertension.

symptoms_or_prerequisites: SBP 140-159 or DBP 90-99 mmHg after lifestyle advice
recommended_action: Start amlodipine 5 mg once daily
exclusions: pregnancy - avoid ACEi/ARB (see card HTN-MED-002)
source_title: Bangladesh Hypertension Guideline (NCDC primary care protocol, Fig. 8)
evidence_passage: If SBP is 140-159 mmHg or DBP 90-99 mmHg -> Advise for lifestyle modification; Review BP after 2 weeks. If SBP is still 140-159 mmHg or DBP 90-99 mmHg, start drug treatment as below. Start amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
linked_facts: Target <140/90 most patients; <130/80 high risk p.9

symptoms_or_prerequisites: treatment not at target after step 1
recommended_action: Step 2: add losartan 50 mg once daily to amlodipine 5 mg; Step 3: add hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily; Step 4: refer to specialist
exclusions: women of childbearing age who may become pregnant - do not prescribe losartan or any ACEi/ARB
source_title: Bangladesh Hypertension Guideline (NCDC primary care protocol, Fig. 8)
evidence_passage: Step 2: amlodipine 5 mg + losartan 50 mg once daily. Step 3: amlodipine 5 mg + losartan 50 mg + hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Step 4: refer to a specialist. DO NOT PRESCRIBE losartan or any ACEi or ARB to women who may become pregnant.
linked_facts: Check serum creatinine and potassium before starting and within 1-2 weeks p.8 footnote

recommended_action: Lifestyle advice: avoid tobacco and alcohol (including second-hand smoke); exercise 2.5 hours/week; eat >=5 servings fruit/vegetables per day; reduce salt to <5 g/day; reduce saturated fat; avoid sugary drinks; monthly follow-up until target then 3-6 monthly; goal BP <140/90 (most) and <130/80 (high risk) within 3 months
source_title: Bangladesh Hypertension Guideline (NCDC primary care protocol, Fig. 8)
evidence_passage: Advice for lifestyle modification: Avoid tobacco and alcohol, including second-hand smoke; Exercise 2.5 hours/week; Eat 5 servings of fruit and/or vegetables on average per day; Reduce salt to less than 5 grams per day; Reduce saturated fat; Limit meal size to one or less; Avoid processed food and sugary drinks;

recommended_action: Assess dehydration and assign Plan: Plan C if one or more danger signs (lethargic/unconscious, absent/weak pulse, respiratory distress) OR >=2 of (sunken eyes, not able to drink/drinks poorly, skin pinch very slow); Plan B if no danger signs AND >=2 of (irritable/restless, sunken eyes, rapid pulse, thirsty/drinks eagerly, skin pinch slow); Plan A if no dehydration signs
exclusions: manage outside cholera pathway if case definition not met
evidence_passage: Severe dehydration: One or more danger signs: Lethargic or unconscious; Absent or weak pulse; Respiratory distress OR at least 2 of the following: Sunken eyes; Not able to drink or drinks poorly; Skin pinch goes back very slowly. Some dehydration: No danger signs AND at least 2 of the following: Irritable or restless; Sunken eyes; Rapid pulse; Thirsty (drinks eagerly); Skin pinch goes back slowly.

recommended_action: Monitor blood glucose for hypoglycaemia and treat rapidly; recheck glucose after 30 min
evidence_passage: Watch for signs of hypoglycaemia and treat rapidly

recommended_action: Give antibiotics: preferred doxycycline single dose (200 mg if <12 years; 300 mg if older children/adults); alternative azithromycin single dose (20 mg/kg if <12 years; 1 g if older children/adults)
exclusions: antibiotics not indicated for non-severe cases unless pregnant/elderly
evidence_passage: Antibiotics for all patients with severe dehydration, pregnant women and the elderly: Preferred is doxycycline single dose (200 mg for under 12 years, or 300 mg for older children and adults. Alternative is azithromycin single dose (20 mg/kg for under 12 years, or 1 g for older children and adults.
linked_facts: Antibiotics for all pregnant women and elderly regardless of hydration status p.5

recommended_action: Give zinc for 10 days: 10 mg once daily if <6 months; 20 mg once daily if >=6 months
evidence_passage: Zinc - give for 10 days: In patients under 6 months, 10mg once per day; In patients over 6 months, 20mg once per day

recommended_action: Give Ringer's lactate IV immediately: under 1 year - 30 mL/kg in 1 hour then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours; all others - 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes then 70 mL/kg in 2.5 hours; use large cannulas or 2 IV lines; write start time on IV bag; give ORS to replace ongoing losses as soon as safe to drink
exclusions: watch for hypoglycaemia and treat rapidly
evidence_passage: Treatment for Severe dehydration Start intravenous fluids immediately: Infants (<12 months): first give 30 mL/kg in 1 hour then give 70 mL/kg in 5 hours; All others (<12 months +): 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes then 70 mL/kg in 2 1/2 hours. Ringers lactate is the first choice.

recommended_action: Provide at least 4 packets of ORS; ensure caregivers know to seek care if >=3 episodes of diarrhoea in 24 h; teach cholera prevention; complete 10 days zinc in children
evidence_passage: Ensure patients and their caregivers understand that anyone with at least 3 episodes of diarrhoea in 24 hours should seek treatment... Provide at least 4 packets of ORS for all patients who are discharged to use at home... For paediatric patients give sufficient zinc to complete 10 days treatment.
linked_facts: Reassess and consider discharge criteria p.1

symptoms_or_prerequisites: severe arthralgia/arthritis not explained by other conditions
recommended_action: Suspect chikungunya fever; categorize as possible (clinical only), probable (clinical + epidemiological: residence/visit to epidemic area within 15 days prior to onset), or confirmed (laboratory criteria)
exclusions: dengue not yet ruled out - manage as dengue until excluded
evidence_passage: Chikungunya Fever should be suspected when a person develops sudden onset of fever, joint manifestations and rash... Possible case: a patient meeting only clinical criteria; Probable case: a patient meeting both the clinical and epidemiological criteria; Confirmed case: a patient meeting the laboratory criteria

recommended_action: Consider dengue in differential: chikungunya more likely with high fever, severe polyarthralgia, arthritis, rash, lymphopenia; dengue more likely with neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hemorrhage, shock
exclusions: do not use clinical findings alone to rule out dengue
evidence_passage: Chikungunya virus more likely to cause high fever, severe polyarthralgia, arthritis, rash, and lymphopenia. Dengue virus more likely to cause neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hemorrhage, shock, and death. Patients with suspected chikungunya should be managed as dengue until dengue has been ruled out.

recommended_action: Routine: CBC (leucopenia, rarely thrombocytopenia), ESR (elevated), CRP (increased in acute phase), SGPT (elevated); specific: RT-PCR within 5 days of onset, IgM 5-28 days after onset, IgG four-fold rise >=3 weeks apart
exclusions: ICT kit for IgM/IgG has very poor diagnostic validity
evidence_passage: Routine Laboratory Investigations: CBC - Leucopenia; Thrombocytopenia: rare; ESR: Usually Elevated; C-Reactive Protein: Increased during the Acute Phase... SGPT: Elevated. Specific Laboratory Investigations: at least one of the following tests in the acute phase: Virus isolation by Cell Culture; RT-PCR (Within 5 days of onset of Illness); IgM antibody in single serum sample collected within 5 to 28 days of onset; Four-fold Rise of IgG antibody in samples collected at least three weeks apart

symptoms_or_prerequisites: no pre-existing liver or kidney disease
recommended_action: Paracetamol up to 1000 mg four times daily in adults; children 50-60 mg/kg/day in divided doses
exclusions: avoid aspirin/NSAIDs during first 10 days until dengue adequately excluded
evidence_passage: Take paracetamol tablets during periods of fever (up to 1000 mg tablets four times daily), in persons with no preexisting liver or kidney disease. Children may be given 50-60 mg per kg body weight per day in divided doses.

symptoms_or_prerequisites: dengue adequately excluded (NS1 negative, afebrile >=48 h, no warning signs)
recommended_action: NSAIDs may be prescribed by physician after 7-10 days of acute phase once dengue is excluded; for refractory arthralgia consider hydroxychloroquine 200 mg orally once daily or chloroquine phosphate 300 mg/day for 4 weeks
exclusions: dengue not excluded
acute phase
evidence_passage: After 7-10 days of acute phase, NSAID can be prescribe by physician if dengue is excluded (NS1 antigen for Dengue is negative, afebrile period of atleast 48 hours and no warning or danger sign of dengue)

recommended_action: Home care: ~2 L oral fluids with electrolytes/24h; rest in warm environment; cold compresses for joints (avoid heat in acute stage); antihistamines for itching; avoid aspirin/NSAIDs; mild exercise/physiotherapy in recovery
exclusions: severe disease -> hospital management
evidence_passage: Consume plenty of water with electrolytes (approximately 2 litres of home available fluids with salt in 24 hours)... Cold compresses may help in reducing joint damage. Heat may increase/worsen joint pain and is therefore best to avoid during acute stage... Antihistamines can be used for itching.

symptoms_or_prerequisites: chikungunya patient with any of the admission criteria
recommended_action: Admit to hospital if: hemodynamically unstable (syncope, SBP <90 mmHg or pulse pressure <30 mmHg), oliguria (<500 mL/24h), altered sensorium, bleeding manifestations, persistent joint pain/disabling arthritis after 3 days symptomatic treatment, age >60 years, infants <1 year, pregnancy, or high-risk group
evidence_passage: Admission criteria: If the person is hemo-dynamically unstable (frequent syncopal attacks, hypotension with a systolic BP less than 90 mmHg or a pulse pressure less than 30 mmHg); oliguria (urine output less than 500 ml in 24 hours); altered sensorium; bleeding manifestations; persons not responding or having persistent joint pain or disabling arthritis even after three days of symptomatic treatment; persons above sixty years; infants (below one year of age); Pregnancy; High risk Group
